items.stem: During a PLC scan cycle, in what order does the controller normally operate?

options.text: Read inputs, execute the program, then update outputs
options.rationale: Correct: the standard scan reads inputs, solves logic, then writes outputs, and repeats.

options.text: Update outputs, read inputs, then execute the program
options.rationale: Outputs are written after logic runs, not first.

options.text: Execute the program continuously without reading inputs
options.rationale: Inputs are sampled each scan; logic is not run on stale-only data.

options.text: Read and write all points at exactly the same instant
options.rationale: The scan is sequential, not simultaneous.

items.explanation: Correct: the standard scan reads inputs, solves logic, then writes outputs, and repeats.

items.stem: Which TWO statements correctly describe the roles of PLCs and SCADA? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The PLC performs real-time control of the process
options.rationale: Correct: PLCs execute the fast, deterministic control logic at the equipment.

options.text: SCADA provides supervisory monitoring and operator oversight
options.rationale: Correct: SCADA aggregates data and lets operators supervise and set points.

options.text: SCADA replaces the PLC for real-time control loops
options.rationale: SCADA supervises; it does not run the fast control loops itself.

options.text: The PLC is only a display screen for operators
options.rationale: That describes an HMI, not a PLC.

items.explanation: Correct: PLCs execute the fast, deterministic control logic at the equipment.

items.stem: A 4-20 mA transmitter measures 0-100 degC. What temperature does a 12 mA signal represent?

options.rationale: Correct: 12 mA is the midpoint of 4-20 mA, so it maps to 50% of the 0-100 range.
The signal is in mA, not degrees; 12 mA maps to the midpoint of the range.
This miscalculates the linear scaling; 12 mA is exactly mid-range.
12 mA is the midpoint, which is 50 degC, not 60.

items.explanation: Correct: 12 mA is the midpoint of 4-20 mA, so it maps to 50% of the 0-100 range.
